prompts.text: What is prompt caching? Explain in under 55 words.

answers.text: Prompt caching is an optimization where a system stores previously processed prompt parts so repeated requests can reuse cached results. This reduces latency and cost by avoiding re-tokenization or reprocessing of unchanged prompt segments, while still generating new outputs for the latest user inputs.

Prompt caching stores the processed form of repeated prompt portions, like system instructions or long documents, so the model doesn't recompute them on each request. This reduces latency and cost for similar queries, since only the new, changing part of the prompt needs fresh processing.

Prompt caching stores frequently used input text—such as long documents, system instructions, or chat history—in memory. When identical text appears in future queries, the system reuses the cached computation instead of reprocessing it from scratch, significantly reducing response latency and computational costs.

Prompt caching is a technique where an AI system stores previously processed input (like long system prompts or documents) so repeated requests reuse it instead of recomputing. This speeds up responses and lowers costs, since only new or changed parts of the prompt need full processing.
